standard.title: Verbs, tense and adverb groups for precision
standard.description: understand how ideas can be expanded and sharpened through careful choice of verbs, elaborated tenses and a range of adverb groups
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how noun groups can be expanded in a variety of ways to provide a fuller description (AC9E5LA06). They have not yet examined the precision available through verb selection, tense elaboration, or adverb groups as tools for sharpening ideas.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students understand how careful verb choice, elaborated tenses and adverb groups expand and sharpen ideas in texts, and can apply these choices in their own writing.

nodes.label: Precise verb selection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how selecting a precise verb sharpens meaning and reduces the need for additional words.
nodes.minimum_width: Replace at least two general verbs (e.g. 'cut', 'say') with more precise alternatives in provided sentences and explain how the meaning changes.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how precise verb choices (e.g. 'slice', 'dice', 'fillet' vs 'cut') sharpen meaning across different text types; explain how verb precision reduces reliance on adverbs to convey the same information.
wider: Compare verb choices in two information reports on the same topic and analyse how verb precision affects the authority and clarity of the text
Examine verbs of saying in narratives (e.g. 'whispered', 'demanded', 'muttered') and explain what each adds beyond the neutral 'said'
nodes.hinge_reason: Students without a repertoire of precise verbs arrive at Node 3 unable to make meaningful verb-precision choices in their writing — the integration task requires accessible vocabulary stock, not just conceptual understanding.

response_modes.reason: Students need to build a repertoire of precise verb choices before they can deploy them fluently in writing. Accumulating alternatives to common general verbs (cut, say, walk, look) across multiple contexts builds the vocabulary stock needed for AC9E6LY06.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cross-text analysis of verb choice is genuinely rich — students develop vocabulary range and critical awareness of how verb precision signals expertise in curriculum-area writing.
success_criteria: Selects a more precise verb than the general alternative in a given sentence
Explains what additional meaning the precise verb contributes

nodes.label: Elaborated tenses
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the different ways English refers to time using simple present, simple past, and future time expressions, and select the appropriate form for a given purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and explain the difference between simple present tense for present states vs. habitual actions in at least two provided sentences; identify at least one way of referring to future time (using 'will', present tense, or adverbials).
nodes.typical_width: Understand and use the simple present tense for present states, habitual actions, and 'timeless' happenings (as in information reports); understand the range of future time expressions and select the appropriate form for different text types and purposes.
wider: Analyse how tense choices function in information reports vs. narratives vs. procedure texts and explain why different text types use different tense conventions
Investigate how authors deliberately shift tense within a text for effect (e.g. a historical recount that shifts to present tense for dramatic immediacy)

response_modes.reason: Students often treat the simple present as a single tense with one function. The three distinct uses (present state, habitual action, timeless truth) are revealed through varied contexts — each text type makes a different use dominant.

success_criteria: Identifies whether a sentence uses simple present for a present state, habitual action, or timeless truth
Names at least two ways of expressing future time in English and provides an example of each

nodes.label: Adverb groups for precision
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how adverb groups expand and sharpen ideas by adding information about manner, place, time or degree, and can use them to improve the precision of their own writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify adverb groups in at least two provided sentences and explain what type of information each adds (manner, place, time, degree); use one adverb group to improve a provided sentence.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how adverb groups work alongside precise verb and tense choices to sharpen ideas across a range of text types; use adverb groups in writing to add precision about when, where, how and to what extent actions occur.
wider: Edit a piece of own writing to evaluate whether each adverb group adds necessary precision or is redundant given a precise verb choice
Compare adverb group use in procedure texts vs. narratives and explain how the type and placement of adverb groups differs by purpose

response_modes.reason: This node integrates verb precision (Node 1) and tense understanding (Node 2) with adverb group selection — the authoring challenge is coordinating all three to produce precise, varied writing. The components come together in the editing act.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Editing writing using all three tools (verb choice, tense, adverb groups) is rich metalinguistic work that directly prepares students for the complex sentence demands of AC9E6LY06.
success_criteria: Identifies and classifies adverb groups by type (manner, place, time, degree) in provided text
Uses at least one adverb group appropriately in own writing to add precision
